findings.what: ROOT CAUSE OF THE BREACH - THE STEP 0 MUTEX DOES NOT ACTUALLY HOLD. process-registry keys locks/check-ins to the acquiring OS PID, but each registry call here is its own short-lived `node -e` process that exits immediately, so the registry reaps the entry as dead within seconds. Verified directly: acquireLock returned true and the lock was visible IN-PROCESS, yet a later getStatus showed locks without gm-site-optimizer and zero gm-site-optimizer process entries. The Step 0 lock therefore provides NO mutual exclusion for an agent-driven run whose steps span many processes - it is a no-op that reads as a success.
findings.decision: no repo change from this run (health mode, and this is a ROUTINE/tooling fix, not P0 site breakage). ESCALATED to Yorkis - this is the defect that let two instances run at once and it will recur every time two runs overlap.
